155	Per-type analysis on MAVEN reveals an anomalous \emph{positive} BCS--F1 correlation (Qwen3 $\rho = +0.184$, $p = 0.025$; MiniLM $\rho = +0.208$, $p = 0.011$). This traces to same-domain embedding collapse \cite{cai-isotropy-clusters-2021}: MAVEN's FrameNet-derived types cluster tightly, so mean BCS conflates confusability with centrality---high-BCS types are semantically central and easy to extract. Controlling for log frequency and degree centrality, the positive correlation vanishes ($p > 0.2$; Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_residualized_bcs}). The pairwise SCS signal remains intact ($r = 0.129$, $p < 10^{-10}$; Table~\ref{tab:pairwise}); the problem is per-type aggregation, not the underlying relationship. Few-NERD's cross-domain schema does not exhibit this confound ($\rho = -0.293$, $p = 0.02$). Mean BCS is thus reliable only for cross-domain schemas; same-domain schemas require pairwise SCS or centrality adjustment.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{llrrrrr}
\toprule
\textbf{Dataset} & \textbf{Embed.} & \textbf{$n$ pairs} & \textbf{$r$} & \textbf{$r^2$} & \textbf{95\% CI} & \textbf{$p$} \\
\midrule
Few-NERD & Qwen3 & 1{,}953 & 0.112 & 0.013 & {[}0.076, 0.156{]} & $7{\times}10^{-7}$ \\
FewRel & Qwen3 & 3{,}160 & 0.187 & 0.035 & {[}0.145, 0.231{]} & $3{\times}10^{-26}$ \\
MAVEN & MiniLM & 11{,}026 & 0.129 & 0.017 & {[}0.104, 0.156{]} & $7{\times}10^{-42}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\caption{Pairwise SCS--confusion correlation. $r^2$ indicates the fraction of variance in type confusion explained by embedding similarity. All three correlations are modest in magnitude but robust across datasets and embedding models (all $p \ll 0.001$). FewRel's balanced design (700 instances per type) eliminates frequency as a confound on its pairwise signal. Confusion rate for each ordered pair $(t_i, t_j)$ is computed as the total bidirectional confusion count $C(t_i{\to}t_j) + C(t_j{\to}t_i)$ divided by the sum of gold frequencies, aggregated over all count conditions; CIs are pair-level percentile bootstrap ($B{=}1{,}000$).}
\label{tab:pairwise}
\end{table}

The correlations are statistically significant but modest: $r^2 \approx 1.3\text{--}3.5\%$. Type-level cluster bootstrap yields wider but still significant CIs (Few-NERD: [0.069, 0.219]; MAVEN: [0.081, 0.185]; $B = 10{,}000$). All three datasets show significant positive correlations between pairwise SCS and type confusion rates. Spearman correlations corroborate: $\rho = 0.144\text{--}0.227$ across all pairs, strengthening to $\rho = 0.27\text{--}0.31$ among pairs with nonzero confusion (though conditioning on the dependent variable may inflate this).

The remaining ${\sim}$98--99\% of variance likely reflects entity frequency, prompt position effects \cite{lost-in-middle-2024}, mention ambiguity, and type definition quality. We frame pairwise SCS as one specific, actionable mechanism---semantic overlap between type labels is directly amenable to schema design---rather than the totality of degradation. Although pairwise $r^2$ is modest, the signal compounds at the batch level into quartile gaps of 3.9--5.3\,pp under typical batching, reaching 31.2\,pp only under extreme-batch construction ($-$25.5\,pp under v2 prompts; typical-batch gap ${\approx}\,2\text{--}4$\,pp, \S\ref{sec:practical_magnitude}).
